*****Rare. Seen near parking lot, at the very top of some dead, scraggly pines. First thought to be an Eastern wood-pewee, but was looked at more closely in the field and realized to be a probably Olive-sided. We contacted Kathy Rigling and a group of other birders who we had seen at Mead earlier. When they arrived, the flycatcher had flown off, but we relocated it about 40  min later where we were able to see it again. Subsequently seen by many over the next few hours and into the morning of the next day. This establishes the first record of this species in Orange county in 17 years since Harry Robinson observed one during his survey of Lake Apopka in 2005.
